sanskrit: uktavākyaṃ tu rājānaṃ kṛpayā kuśikātmajaḥ abravīn madhuraṃ vākyaṃ sākṣāc caṇḍālarūpiṇam
english: Having heard the king's words, the son of Kuśika, moved by compassion, spoke sweetly to the one who stood before him in the very form of a caṇḍāla.

sanskrit: ikṣvāko svāgataṃ vatsa jānāmi tvāṃ sudhārmikam śaraṇaṃ te bhaviṣyāmi mā bhaiṣīr nṛpapuṃgava
english: "Welcome, dear child of the Ikṣvāku line — I know you to be one of true righteousness. I shall be your refuge; fear not, O bull among kings."

sanskrit: aham āmantraye sarvān maharṣīn puṇyakarmaṇaḥ yajñasāhyakarān rājaṃs tato yakṣyasi nirvṛtaḥ
english: "I shall invite all the great seers of meritorious deeds who can assist in the sacrifice; then, O king, you shall perform the rite in peace."

sanskrit: guruśāpakṛtaṃ rūpaṃ yad idaṃ tvayi vartate anena saha rūpeṇa saśarīro gamiṣyasi
english: "This form that rests upon you, wrought by your guru's curse — in this very form, with this very body, you shall go to heaven."

sanskrit: hastaprāptam ahaṃ manye svargaṃ tava nareśvara yas tvaṃ kauśikam āgamya śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "I deem heaven to be already in the palm of your hand, O lord of men — for you have come to Kauśika, who is worthy of refuge, and taken shelter with him."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ putrān paramadhārmikān vyādideśa mahāprājñān yajñasaṃbhārakāraṇāt
english: Having spoken thus, the greatly resplendent one gave instructions to his sons, who were supremely righteous and exceedingly wise, for the gathering of all that was needed for the sacrifice.

sanskrit: sarvāñ śiṣyān samāhūya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Summoning all his disciples together, he spoke these words to them.

sanskrit: sarvān ṛṣivarān vatsā ānayadhvaṃ mamājñayā saśiṣyān suhṛdaś caiva sartvijaḥ subahuśrutān
english: "Bring hither, dear ones, all the foremost seers, by my command — along with their disciples, friends, and officiating priests who are versed in the sacred texts."

sanskrit: yad anyo vacanaṃ brūyān madvākyabalacoditaḥ tat sarvam akhilenoktaṃ mamākhyeyam anādṛtam
english: "Whatever any one of them may say when urged by the force of my words — all of it, whatever is spoken disparagingly, is to be reported to me in full."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā diśo jagmus tadājñayā ājagmur atha deśebhyaḥ sarvebhyo brahmavādinaḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, the disciples set out in all directions by his command; and from every region came the knowers of Brahman.

sanskrit: te ca śiṣyāḥ samāgamya muniṃ jvalitatejasaṃ ūcuś ca vacanaṃ sarve sarveṣāṃ brahmavādinām
english: Those disciples, having assembled, all reported to the sage, who blazed with splendour, the words of all the Brahman-speakers.

sanskrit: śrutvā te vacanaṃ sarve samāyānti dvijātayaḥ sarvadeśeṣu cāgacchan varjayitvā mahodayam
english: Having heard the message, all the twice-born come — they arrived from every region, all excepting Mahodaya.

sanskrit: vāsiṣṭhaṃ tac chataṃ sarvaṃ krodhaparyākulākṣaram yad āha vacanaṃ sarvaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ munipuṃgava
english: "Hear, O bull among sages, all that which the entire hundred of the Vāsiṣṭhas said — every word they spoke, their eyes agitated with anger."

sanskrit: kṣatriyo yājako yasya caṇḍālasya viśeṣataḥ kathaṃ sadasi bhoktāro havis tasya surarṣayaḥ
english: "The officiating priest of this man is a kṣatriya — and more particularly, he is a caṇḍāla. How then can the divine seers be partakers of the oblations at that assembly?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā vā mahātmāno bhuktvā caṇḍālabhojanam kathaṃ svargaṃ gamiṣyanti viśvāmitreṇa pālitāḥ
english: "Or how shall the great-souled brāhmaṇas, having eaten the food of a caṇḍāla under the superintendence of Viśvāmitra, attain heaven?"

sanskrit: etad vacanaṃ naiṣṭhuryam ūcuḥ saṃraktalocanāḥ vāsiṣṭhā muniśārdūla sarve te samahodayāḥ
english: These harsh words were spoken, their eyes red with passion, by all the Vāsiṣṭhas together with Mahodaya, O tiger among sages.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ munipuṃgavaḥ krodhasaṃraktanayanaḥ saroṣam idam abravīt
english: Having heard those words of all of them, the bull among sages, his eyes flushed red with wrath, spoke in great anger.

sanskrit: yad dūṣayanty aduṣṭaṃ māṃ tapa ugraṃ samāsthitam bhasmībhūtā durātmāno bhaviṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: "These evil-souled ones who revile me, blameless as I am and engaged in fierce austerity — they shall be reduced to ashes, of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: adya te kālapāśena nītā vaivasvatakṣayam saptajātiśatāny eva mṛtapāḥ santu sarvaśaḥ
english: "This very day, led away by the noose of Kāla to the realm of Vaivasvata, may they all drink of the bitter cup through seven hundred births in every form of existence."

sanskrit: śvamāṃsaniyatāhārā muṣṭikā nāma nirghṛṇāḥ vikṛtāś ca virūpāś ca lokān anucarantv imān
english: "Subsisting always on dog's flesh, pitiless ones known by the name Muṣṭika, disfigured and misshapen — may they wander through these worlds."

sanskrit: mahodayaś ca durbuddhir mām adūṣyaṃ hy adūṣayat dūṣiṭaḥ sarvalokeṣu niṣādatvaṃ gamiṣyati
english: "And Mahodaya, that evil-minded one, has reviled me though I am beyond reproach; fallen from esteem in all the worlds, he shall attain the state of a Niṣāda."

sanskrit: prāṇātipātanirato niranukrośatāṃ gataḥ dīrghakālaṃ mama krodhād durgatiṃ vartayiṣyati
english: "Devoted to the taking of life, having abandoned all compassion, he shall, by my wrath, dwell in misfortune for a very long time."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ virarāma mahātejā ṛṣimadhye mahāmuniḥ
english: Having spoken this much, Viśvāmitra, the great ascetic, of mighty splendour, that great sage, fell silent in the midst of the seers.

sanskrit: tapobalahatān kṛtvā vāsiṣṭhān samahodayān ṛṣimadhye mahātejā viśvāmitro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Having struck down the Vāsiṣṭhas together with Mahodaya by the force of his austerity, the greatly resplendent Viśvāmitra then addressed the assembly of seers.

sanskrit: ayam ikṣvākudāyādas triśaṅkur iti viśrutaḥ dharmiṣṭhaś ca vadānyaś ca māṃ caiva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ svenānena śarīreṇa devalokajigīṣayā
english: "This descendant of the Ikṣvāku line, celebrated as Triśaṅku, is most righteous and most generous; he has come to me as his refuge, desiring to win the world of the gods in this very body."

sanskrit: yathāyaṃ svaśarīreṇa devalokaṃ gamiṣyati tathā pravartyatāṃ yajño bhavadbhiś ca mayā saha
english: "In such a manner that this man may ascend to the divine world in his own body — let the sacrifice be conducted by you together with me."

sanskrit: viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā sarva eva maharṣayaḥ ūcuḥ sametya sahitā dharmajñā dharmasaṃhitam
english: Having heard the words of Viśvāmitra, all the great seers, gathered together, those who knew the dharma, spoke what was in accord with dharma.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kuśikadāyādo muniḥ paramakopanaḥ yad āha vacanaṃ samyag etat kāryaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: "This descendant of Kuśika is a sage of supreme wrathfulness; what he has said is right — this must be done, without doubt."

sanskrit: agnikalpo hi bhagavāñ śāpaṃ dāsyati roṣitaḥ tasmāt pravartyatāṃ yajñaḥ saśarīro yathā divam gacched ikṣvākudāyādo viśvāmitrasya tejasā
english: "For the venerable one, resembling fire, will give a curse when provoked. Therefore let the sacrifice be conducted, so that the descendant of the Ikṣvāku line may ascend to heaven in his own body by the might of Viśvāmitra."

sanskrit: tataḥ pravartyatāṃ yajñaḥ sarve samadhitiṣṭhate
english: "Therefore let the sacrifice proceed; let all take up their respective offices."

sanskrit: evam uktvā maharṣayaḥ saṃjahrus tāḥ kriyās tadā yājakāś ca mahātejā viśvāmitro 'bhavat kratau
english: Having spoken thus, the great seers took up all the rites, and the greatly resplendent Viśvāmitra himself became the chief officiant at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: ṛtvijaś cānupūrvyeṇa mantravan mantrakovidāḥ cakruḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi yathākalpaṃ yathāvidhi
english: And the officiating priests, one after another, all versed in sacred formulas, performed all the rites with mantras, according to prescription and proper procedure.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena mahatā viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ cakārāvāhanaṃ tatra bhāgārthaṃ sarvadevatāḥ
english: Then, after a great stretch of time, Viśvāmitra of great austerity invoked all the gods to come there for their shares of the oblation.

sanskrit: nāhyāgamaṃs tadāhūtā bhāgārthaṃ sarvadevatāḥ tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo viśvamitro mahāmuniḥ
english: But though thus invoked, none of the gods came to receive their portions. Then the great sage Viśvāmitra was seized by anger.

sanskrit: sruvam udyamya sakrodhas triśaṅkum idam abravīt paśya me tapaso vīryaṃ svārjitasya nareśvara
english: Raising the sacrificial ladle in wrath, he spoke thus to Triśaṅku: "Behold the power of the austerity earned by myself, O lord of men."

sanskrit: eṣa tvāṃ svaśarīreṇa nayāmi svargam ojasā duṣprāpaṃ svaśarīreṇa divaṃ gaccha narādhipa
english: "Now I shall bear you to heaven in your own body by my own might. Go to the sky in your own body, O ruler of men — that which is hard to attain in one's own body."

sanskrit: svārjitaṃ kiṃ cid apy asti mayā hi tapasaḥ phalam rājaṃs tvaṃ tejasā tasya saśarīro divaṃ vraja
english: "Whatever fruit of austerity earned by myself there is — by the might of that fruit, O king, ascend to heaven in this very body."

sanskrit: uktavākye munau tasmin saśarīro nareśvaraḥ divaṃ jagāma kākutstha munīnāṃ paśyatāṃ tadā
english: When the sage had so spoken, the lord of men ascended to heaven in his own body, O Kākutstha, while the assembled sages looked on.

sanskrit: devalokagataṃ dṛṣṭvā triśaṅkuṃ pākaśāsanaḥ saha sarvaiḥ suragaṇair idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing Triśaṅku arrived at the divine world, Pākaśāsana — Indra — along with all the hosts of gods, spoke these words.

sanskrit: triśaṅko gaccha bhūyas tvaṃ nāsi svargakṛtālayaḥ guruśāpahato mūḍha pata bhūmim avākśirāḥ
english: "Triśaṅku, go back — you have no right to abode in heaven. You fool, struck down by your guru's curse, fall headlong to the earth."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahendreṇa triśaṅkur apatat punaḥ vikrośamānas trāhīti viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam
english: Thus addressed by Mahendra, Triśaṅku fell back down, crying out "Save me! Save me!" to Viśvāmitra, that treasury of austerity.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya krośamānasya kauśikaḥ roṣam āhārayat tīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Hearing the cry of that falling man, Kauśika gathered fierce wrath and called out, "Stop! Stop!"

sanskrit: ṛṣimadhye sa tejasvī prajāpatir ivāparaḥ sṛjan dakṣiṇamārgasthān saptarṣīn aparān punaḥ
english: That resplendent one, like a second Prajāpati, in the midst of the seers, began creating a new set of seven sages established along the southern path.

sanskrit: nakṣatramālām aparām asṛjat krodhamūrchitaḥ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āsthāya munimadhye mahāyaśāḥ
english: Inflamed by anger, the greatly renowned one created a new garland of stars, taking the southern direction as his orientation, in the midst of the seers.

sanskrit: sṛṣṭvā nakṣatravaṃśaṃ ca krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ anyam indraṃ kariṣyāmi loko vā syād anindrakaḥ daivatāny api sa krodhāt sraṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Having created the stellar lineage, darkened by wrath, he declared: "I shall create another Indra — or let the world exist without one." And in his anger he began to create the very gods as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃbhrāntāḥ sarṣisaṃghāḥ surarṣabhāḥ viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānam ūcuḥ sānunayaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then the bulls among gods, the hosts of seers, all exceedingly agitated, spoke words of supplication to the great-souled Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: ayaṃ rājā mahābhāga guruśāpaparikṣataḥ saśarīro divaṃ yātuṃ nārhaty eva tapodhana
english: "This king, O greatly fortunate one, O treasury of austerity, struck down by his guru's curse, is indeed not fit to go to heaven in his own body."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ munipuṃgavaḥ abravīt sumahad vākyaṃ kauśikaḥ sarvadevatāḥ
english: Having heard those words of the gods, Kauśika, the bull among sages, spoke very great words to all the deities.

sanskrit: saśarīrasya bhadraṃ vas triśaṅkor asya bhūpateḥ ārohaṇaṃ pratijñāya nānṛtaṃ kartum utsahe
english: "I have given my pledge that this lord of the earth, Triśaṅku, would ascend in his own body — I am not able to make that pledge false. May it be well with you all."

sanskrit: sargo 'stu saśarīrasya triśaṅkor asya śāśvataḥ nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi māmakāni dhruvāṇy atha
english: "Let there be a realm for this Triśaṅku in his own body, and let it be eternal; and let all my stars remain fixed and firm."

sanskrit: yāval lokā dhariṣyanti tiṣṭhantv etāni sarvaśaḥ matkṛtāni surāḥ sarve tad anujñātum arhatha
english: "For as long as the worlds shall endure, let all these creations of mine stand firm throughout. O gods, all of you ought to sanction this."

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ surāḥ sarve pratyūcur munipuṃgavam
english: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to the bull among sages.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te tiṣṭhantv etāni sarvaśaḥ gagane tāny anekāni vaiśvānarapathād bahiḥ
english: "So be it. May it be well with you. Let all these many creations stand firm in the sky, beyond the path of Vaiśvānara — the fire."

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇi muniśreṣṭha teṣu jyotiḥṣu jājvalan avākśirās triśaṅkuś ca tiṣṭhatv amarasaṃnibhaḥ
english: "O foremost of sages, let the stars stand, and among those luminaries blazing with light, let Triśaṅku too stand — head downward — resembling an immortal."

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu dharmātmā sarvadevair abhiṣṭutaḥ ṛṣibhiś ca mahātejā bāḍham ity āha devatāḥ
english: Then Viśvāmitra, righteous in soul, praised by all the gods and by the seers, the greatly resplendent one, said to the deities: "So be it."

sanskrit: tato devā mahātmāno munayaś ca tapodhanāḥ jagmur yathāgataṃ sarve yajñasyānte narottama
english: Then all the great-souled gods and the sages, those treasuries of austerity, departed just as they had come, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, O best of men.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro mahātmātha prasthitān prekṣya tān ṛṣīn abravīn naraśārdūla sarvāṃs tān vanavāsinaḥ
english: Then the great-souled Viśvāmitra, watching those seers depart, spoke to all those forest-dwelling sages, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: mahāvighnaḥ pravṛtto 'yaṃ dakṣiṇām āsthito diśam diśam anyāṃ prapatsyāmas tatra tapsyāmahe tapaḥ
english: "A great obstruction has arisen, stationed in the southern direction; let us set out for another direction — there we shall practise austerity."

sanskrit: paścimāyāṃ viśālāyāṃ puṣkareṣu mahātmanaḥ sukhaṃ tapaś cariṣyāmaḥ paraṃ tad dhi tapovanam
english: "In the vast western region, in the sacred tīrthas of Puṣkara, we shall comfortably practise great austerity — for that is the supreme grove of penance."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ puṣkareṣu mahāmuniḥ tapa ugraṃ durādharṣaṃ tepe mūlaphalāśanaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the greatly resplendent great sage betook himself to Puṣkara and performed fierce, unapproachable austerity, subsisting on roots and fruits.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu ayodhyādhipatir nṛpaḥ ambarīṣa iti khyāto yaṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: At this very time the king who ruled Ayodhyā, known as Ambarīṣa, set about performing a sacrifice.

sanskrit: tasya vai yajamānasya paśum indro jahāra ha pranaṣṭe tu paśau vipro rājānam idam abravīt
english: But from that sacrificer Indra stole the sacrificial animal. When the animal had disappeared, the brāhmaṇa priest spoke these words to the king.

sanskrit: paśur adya hṛto rājan pranaṣṭas tava durnayāt arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ ghnanti doṣā nareśvara
english: "O king, the sacrificial animal has been stolen and lost today through your lack of vigilance. Sins strike a king who does not protect what is entrusted to him, O lord of men."

sanskrit: prāyaścittaṃ mahad dhy etan naraṃ vā puruṣarṣabha ānayasva paśuṃ śīghraṃ yāvat karma pravartate
english: "This requires a great expiation. O bull among men, bring either a man or an animal quickly, before the rite proceeds further."

sanskrit: upādhyāya vacaḥ śrutvā sa rājā puruṣarṣabha anviyeṣa mahābuddhiḥ paśuṃ gobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Hearing the preceptor's words, that king, a bull among men, of great wisdom, sought after the sacrificial victim, offering thousands of cows in exchange.

sanskrit: deśāñ janapadāṃs tāṃs tān nagarāṇi vanāni ca āśramāṇi ca puṇyāni mārgamāṇo mahīpatiḥ
english: The lord of the earth, searching, visited region after region, settlements, cities, forests, and sacred hermitages.

sanskrit: sa putrasahitaṃ tāta sabhāryaṃ raghunandana bhṛgutuṅge samāsīnam ṛcīkaṃ saṃdadarśa ha
english: He then found, O dear one, O delight of the Raghu line, Ṛcīka seated on the hill Bhṛgutuṅga together with his sons and wife.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejāḥ praṇamyābhiprasādya ca brahmarṣiṃ tapasā dīptaṃ rājarṣir amitaprabhaḥ pṛṣṭvā sarvatra kuśalam ṛcīkaṃ tam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: The royal seer of immeasurable splendour, having reverentially saluted and propitiated that brahmarṣi blazing with austerity, and having enquired after his welfare in every respect, spoke these words to Ṛcīka.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasreṇa vikriṇīṣe sutaṃ yadi paśor arthe mahābhāga kṛtakṛtyo 'smi bhārgava
english: "If you would sell a son for a hundred thousand cows for the purpose of the sacrificial animal, O greatly fortunate one, O descendant of Bhṛgu, I shall have fulfilled my purpose."

sanskrit: sarve parisṛtā deśā yajñiyaṃ na labhe paśum dātum arhasi mūlyena sutam ekam ito mama
english: "All regions have been traversed and I have not obtained the required sacrificial animal. You should give one son from among yours here, for the price stated."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahātejā ṛcīkas tv abravīd vacaḥ nāhaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ naraśreṣṭhaṃ vikrīṇīyāṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Thus addressed, the greatly resplendent Ṛcīka spoke: "I would never sell the eldest under any circumstances, O best of men."

sanskrit: ṛcīkasya vacaḥ śrutvā teṣāṃ mātā mahātmanām uvāca naraśārdūlam ambarīṣaṃ tapasvinī
english: Hearing the words of Ṛcīka, the mother of those great-souled sons, the ascetic woman, spoke to Ambarīṣa, that tiger among men.

sanskrit: mamāpi dayitaṃ viddhi kaniṣṭhaṃ śunakaṃ nṛpa
english: "Know also that the youngest, Śunaka, is dear to me, O king."

sanskrit: prāyeṇa hi naraśreṣṭha jyeṣṭhāḥ pitṛṣu vallabhāḥ mātṝṇāṃ ca kanīyāṃsas tasmād rakṣe kanīyasaṃ
english: "For generally, O best of men, the eldest sons are dear to fathers, and the youngest to mothers; therefore I protect the youngest."

sanskrit: uktavākye munau tasmin munipatnyāṃ tathaiva ca śunaḥśepaḥ svayaṃ rāma madhyamo vākyam abravīt
english: When the sage had spoken thus and the sage's wife likewise, the middle son, Śunaḥśepa himself, O Rāma, spoke these words.

sanskrit: pitā jyeṣṭham avikreyaṃ mātā cāha kanīyasaṃ vikrītaṃ madhyamaṃ manye rājan putraṃ nayasva mām
english: "My father says the eldest is not to be sold; my mother says the youngest. I consider the middle son sold — O king, take me away."

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasreṇa śunaḥśepaṃ nareśvaraḥ gṛhītvā paramaprīto jagāma raghunandana
english: The lord of men, taking Śunaḥśepa for a hundred thousand cows, departed in great joy, O delight of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: ambarīṣas tu rājarṣī ratham āropya satvaraḥ śunaḥśepaṃ mahātejā jagāmāśu mahāyaśāḥ
english: The royal seer Ambarīṣa, the greatly resplendent one of great renown, having placed Śunaḥśepa on the chariot, departed swiftly.
